_what: How detected events become the parts of a recording that are kept (cut-by-events.mjs). `rules` has one row per event kind: `before` and `after` are the seconds kept around the event's time, `min_confidence` (optional) is a floor for that kind. A kind with no row follows `unknown_kind`: `drop` removes it, `default` uses `default_rule`. Windows closer than `merge_gap_s` become one; a window shorter than `min_window_s` is dropped. Confidence decides what is done with an event: at or above `act_at` it is kept, from `ask_at` up to `act_at` it is returned in `asked` for the person to confirm, below `ask_at` it is abstained and said so. An event with no confidence follows `unscored`: `act` keeps it, `abstain` drops it. A new kind of event (a serve, a goal, a laugh) is a new row; a different detector is a new row in `detectors`. Word, filler and long-pause cuts from a transcript are not here: adopt-visual-content's auto-edit is their single owner (cut-the-action.mjs calls it). A `stream` detector row names a row of `streams`: its encoder turns the recording into feature frames, its core carries a baseline from frame to frame (src/stream-core.mjs) and its heads, rows of their own, say what happened; retuning or swapping a head touches neither the encoder nor the core.

detectors.note: No weights: the loudness rise and the picture change, ranked by find-action-moments.mjs.
No weights: a running baseline of the loudness rise and the picture change; a frame well above what the recording has been like so far is an event. The heads are rows of `streams`.
A model the person's Mac serves answers for stretches of the recording; which model is a row in records/local-model-records.json.

words.no_events: No event was kept, so nothing is cut.
words.abstained: {count} event(s) were left out because they were not certain enough.
words.asked: {count} event(s) need the person to say yes before they are kept.
words.other_device: The event came from a device that is not in this session.

sound-and-motion.note: The core keeps a smoothed mean and variance per feature (alpha is how fast it forgets). A head adds its weighted deviations; at z_min an event is made, at z_full it is certain; refractory_s keeps one hit from being many events.
